title: Why parallel computing: numerical models and their cost
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
lecture_corrections: W3L1: transistor density is said to double 'every 18 months' (stated in two places in the recording). The lecture's own chart caption says 'approximately every two years'. Moore 1965: yearly; Moore 1975: two years expected. Rupp data fit: 27.3 months (1971-1999), 23.9 months (2000-2021). The 18-month figure is Bohr's (2007) figure for Intel transistor counts in the 1970s-1980s only. The 18-month wording rests on the machine transcript alone (it occurs twice and is not a plausible mishearing of 'two years'); the slide caption confirms the two-year figure.
W3L1: 'doubling the power every 18 months' conflates component count with computing power; the listed clock frequency has had a slope of -0.011 doublings per year since 2004.

W3L1: Dennard scaling is said to have broken because a finite voltage is needed to tell 0 from 1. Bohr (2007, p. 12): the threshold voltage cannot scale because of sub-threshold leakage. Refined, not contradicted.

W3L1: the bag-of-integers example is presented as Amdahl's law. Its serial part (adding p partial sums) grows with p; f_eff = p^2/(M(p-1)) is not constant. Pairwise addition changes the result (107 s at p = 100). The conclusion that machines with millions of cores are useless holds only at fixed problem size (Gustafson 1988).

W3L2 slide: the discretized equation is written (T_{i-1,j} - T_{i,j} + T_{i+1,j})/dx^2 + (T_{i,j-1} - T_{i,j} + T_{i,j+1})/dy^2 = 0. The coefficient of the centre value must be -2 in each term; a constant temperature does not satisfy the slide's expression.

W3L2 slide: 'Iterative is more efficient' (than direct). Against banded Cholesky, plain Jacobi needs 10.9-12.8 times the operations (both O(N^4)); iteration wins in memory (N^2 vs N^3) and, for better methods (CG, SOR, multigrid), in operations. Demmel 1995 table.

W3L2: the slide labels three corners T_0 and the bottom-right corner T_inf; the top and left edges are held at T_0 and the right and bottom edges vary from T_0 to T_inf (spoken; the word 'linearly' is spoken only and is not used). T_inf is a symbol, not a value; the chapter uses the book's canonical boundary values (u = 1 on the top edge, 0 elsewhere) and says so.
source_uncertainties: Intel ARK page for the i5-12450H returned HTTP 403 to a scripted request (2026-10-26). Turbo frequencies 4.40 GHz (P-core) and 3.30 GHz (E-core) and the core layout are those recorded in chapter 11; a web search returned TechPowerUp and other secondary sources with the same turbo values. Base frequencies were not used because sources disagree (E-core base 1.3 to 1.7 GHz).

Moore (1965): the Princeton reprint has four pages and prints no issue page numbers; 'p. 2 of 4' is the reprint page. The article starts on p. 114 of the issue according to the Computer History Museum catalogue; the end page 117 was not verified and is not cited.

Dennard et al. (1974): the PDF is a scan with OCR; the OCR of Table I is scrambled, so the factors were taken from the sentences beside the table (delay by K, power per circuit by K^2, power density constant). The printed page 265 was identified from the page text.

Bohr (2007): page numbers are the printed numbers of the SSCS newsletter (article on pp. 11-13); the figures 2x per 18 months and sub-threshold leakage numbers are read from the text, not the figures.

Rupp trend data: retrieved from the master branch on 2026-10-26 (no commit hash recorded); entries mix vendors and product classes; the listing embeds the values rounded to 4 significant digits, so its fits differ from fits of the raw files in the last digits only. The break at 2004 and the start at 1990 are read from the plot; the fit from 2007 (-0.017 per year) shows the sign does not depend on it. The data do not identify causes.
Demmel (1995) lecture notes: the table is in O() notation with N the number of unknowns; used for exponents only. The quotation 'cannot be straightforwardly parallelized' is from the same page.

Saad (2003): the five-point matrix in natural ordering is taken to be consistently ordered (classical result, Young); Definition 4.13 was not checked for it. Exercise 6 relies on the fact only through the measured sweep ratio (0.521-0.530) and the measured centre error factor.
Gustafson (1988) was read from the author's site (3 pages). Goldberg (1991) was read as the Oracle HTML reprint, where formulas are images; epsilon = (beta/2) beta^-p was read from the text.

The GCC manual pages were the current online version on 2026-10-26, which may be newer than gcc 13.3 used for the runs; the 13.3 manual was not opened. The quoted statements on -ftree-parallelize-loops and -march were not tested against 13.3 text.

System V AMD64 ABI draft 0.99.6 (2012) was used; the current psABI version was not opened. Printed page 9 (scope) and the register sequence on p. 124 (Appendix A.2.1) were read from the draft; section numbers are the reliable references.

The stair-step pattern of successive changes (ratios alternating between rho^2 and 1.000000) was observed for N = 31 and is explained only as a candidate (the -rho eigenvalue); it was not derived. That the largest error of the canonical problem is 7.9e-3 at N = 7 and 7.2e-3 at N = 15, 31, 63 is observed for these four sizes only and was not proved to stay constant.

Timing samples (jacobi_time.c, autopar.c) were captured while other agents' jobs ran on the machine. Ranges quoted in the text come from seven runs of the timing listing (time per point update, in cache 1.0-1.6 ns, N = 1000 1.6-2.6 ns; one run under heavy load 4.3-5.3 ns) and six runs of autopar.c, plus an earlier two-run test at N = 1000 and 2000 not reproduced by a listing. A single-thread time is a time on an unknown core of the hybrid processor.

The lecture's 'city' examples are used only as a scale for N: 10 km at 10 m spacing (N = 1000) and at 1 m (N = 10^4) are the chapter's illustration, not the lecture's numbers. Times for N >= 4000 are extrapolations of the measured rate.
The claim '3 nanometer technology' (W3L1) was not checked; the dimension that a node name denotes was not looked up. The modelling error of the W3L2 pipeline is not estimated.

Statements that rest on the machine transcript alone were not recorded as lecture corrections: the clock figures of about 3 GHz and 1.5 GHz, the 50 percent slowdown anecdote, the 'i and j from 0 to n' count and the wording of the Taylor-series passage were not confirmed by a slide. The anecdote is reported as told and is not tested. Timestamps are local segment times and locate topic changes to within a few seconds.

Regime of the single-mode sweep count: k = ln(c/tol)/(-ln rho) with c = (1-rho) 4/pi^2 holds only for tol much smaller than c. At N = 1000 and tol = 1e-6, c = 2.0e-6 and tol/c = 0.50, outside the range; measured sweeps are 1.36 times the count and the centre error 0.77 (largest error 0.82) of the bound rho/(1-rho) tol, identical at N = 63, 127, 255 (listing jacobi.c, last table; the largest-error constant 0.82 comes from a run against a converged solution that is not a listing). The estimates 1.91e5 sweeps and error 0.17 for N = 1000 use these constants; Chapter 4 measured 191,001 sweeps and maximum error 0.167 (not re-run here). The cost table (cost_model.py) uses the error-based count with eps, which is in range.

Length: about 14,000 words of prose with each inline formula counted as one token (about 13,000 with formulas removed), against the brief's 6,000-9,000; two trimming passes were made and the reviewer may cut further.

Maximum-norm guarantee: the largest row sum of G(Id-G)^-1 is 1.454 times rho/(1-rho) (computed from the matrix at N = 7, 15, 31 and by iteration at N = 63, reviewer's value 74.2/300.5/1205.8); not a listing. Chapter 4 states the same factor.

Auto-parallelization: the -fopt-info-loop report for autopar.c names only the top-edge fill in main (line 40); the sweep contains no OpenMP runtime call (objdump). The runs of autopar.c show the automatic build inside the plain build's range for that reason.

B4: Exercise 1 ranges, step 2 in k, 7.9e-3 at N = 7, Exercise 4 value 5176.
